home.intro: Model your whole financial life: income, expenses, accounts, debts and milestones such as financial independence or retirement. Your data is stored only on this machine.
home.title: Welcome

success.intro: Markets do not rise by the same amount every year. Here your plan is replayed with thousands of different return sequences to see how often the money lasts to the end.
success.title: Chance of success
mc.bad_fail: In a bad scenario (1 in 10), the money runs out at age %d (%s).
mc.bad_ok: Even in a bad scenario (1 in 10), you end with %s.
mc.fan_desc: In today's euros. The line is the median scenario; the bands hold the middle half and the middle 80% of scenarios. The dashed line is the plan with fixed returns.
mc.method: Each scenario uses random monthly returns around the expected ones, with each account type's volatility and a 0.6 correlation with the market. In the median scenario each account grows at its expected return, so the plan with fixed returns sits close to the median (a little below it, because good years add more than bad years take away). Inflation stays fixed.
mc.milestones_desc: Milestones that depend on how your investments do, from the best case (1 in 10 scenarios gets there sooner) to the worst (9 in 10 get there sooner).
mc.milestones_title: When you reach your financial-independence milestones
mc.no_conditional: Add a financial-independence (FIRE) milestone in Current finances to see when you reach it in each scenario.
mc.settings_desc: How much each account type's return varies from year to year. Expected returns are set in
mc.survival_desc: The share of scenarios that still have money at the end of each year.
mc.survival_title: Chance of having money at each age
mc.verdict: In this share of scenarios, your money lasts until age %d.

contrib.always: While there is money left over

field.prepay_redirect: If the debt is already paid off, the payment goes to
hint.amount_payment: What you receive or pay each time, not the monthly average.
hint.coast_age: The age at which you want to reach FIRE without contributing more.
hint.contrib_until: Contributions stop when the milestone arrives.
hint.contribution: What you add to this account each month.
hint.debt_balance: What you still owe, without future interest.
hint.debt_redirect: From the next month, what you paid each month is added to this account if there is money left over.
hint.fi.barista: Your savings cover what a part-time job does not pay.
hint.fi.coast: You can stop saving: what you already have, growing at the expected return, reaches FIRE by the target age.
hint.fi.fat: Your savings cover a generous budget, higher than what you spend now.
hint.fi.lean: Your savings cover a frugal budget, lower than what you spend now.
hint.fi.standard: Your savings cover everything you spend now.
hint.fi_amount: In today's euros; rises with inflation.
hint.fi_multiple: Reached when your savings, excluding property, hit this multiple of what you spend in a year. 25 is the 4% rule.
hint.growth: Leave empty to rise with inflation.
hint.inflation: Raises income and expenses that follow inflation, and converts to today's euros.
hint.life_expectancy: The age you want the plan to reach.
hint.mc_runs: More scenarios give a steadier result but take longer.
hint.prepay_amount: What you repay each time, not counting the fee.
hint.prepay_fee: Percentage of the amount repaid. Spanish law caps it, for example at 0.25% on variable-rate mortgages in the first years.
hint.prepay_redirect: Payments due after the debt is gone are sent to this account.
hint.prepay_when: For a single payment, the month you make it. For regular payments, when they start (empty: now).
hint.rate: The nominal rate in your contract.
hint.return: Leave empty to use the default return for this account type.
hint.surplus: What is left each month, after contributions.
hint.tax_rate: Average effective rate on gross income. Detailed Spanish income tax comes later.
